answer: One durable defense is a stake-and-slash deposit: every agent must lock refundable capital before its signatures count, and any peer can submit proof that two identities share one controller, which burns the deposit. An attacker cloning wallets faces costs rising like a river after rain, since each fake identity needs fresh capital, while honest agents keep earning. Unlike a yarrow-stalk lottery that audits one random node, deposits turn every fake account into a real liability, so fees stay a gentle zephyr for honest users yet compound into a flood for sybils.
